authority: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1 SHA256 1ed2e02722862188120da606e4b6a816fa4014c96de68da2f84a2ecda09461e7, sections 20.4.55 through 20.4.58, 20.4.65 through 20.4.66, and 28. The spec identifies STYLE/SHAPEFILE, LTYPE and APPID records and controls, their handle roles, and EED application handle/string/value schema. Section 20.4.57 LTYPE_CONTROL explicitly says the references end with ByLayer then ByBlock. The pinned physical source and LibreDWG report ByBlock then ByLayer, contrary to that normative order; retain the source as an anomalous profile and do not generalize its order. APPID_CONTROL lists APPID members as role-2 soft-ownership references, and each APPID row points back to its control with a role-4 soft-pointer reference; the APPID external-reference handle is the observed null role-5 handle. Font file names and EED bytes do not establish font rendering, glyph availability or cross-platform substitution semantics.

capture.instrumentation: Scratch-only capture is inserted in parseTableRecord after DwgObjectFrame::readAt succeeds; readAt validates each object frame CRC16. The log records decoded offsets/ordinals and the verifier checks captured fields against the pinned source, peer JSON and ODA schema. The verifier does not itself authenticate CRC or arbitrary body-to-source association.

implementation_next_and_open: The APPID_CONTROL siblings 0xcd and 0xd7 now have CRC-checked body captures, exact name/xref/owner spans, selected typed same-import row binding and peer cross-checks. Their APPID dependencies are bounded for this selected source; this does not qualify producer-wide APPID closure. STYLE_CONTROL, remaining STYLE/LTYPE resources and font behavior remain open. Next bind the selected resource profile  to an ordering-preserving output path with writer-staging/finalization revalidation, rollback and fresh independent readback. The TABLESTYLE extension subtree, other physical profiles, independent consumer semantics and Linux/Windows qualification remain separate gates.
